annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "Earwicker" on page 70 within "The Trial of HCE": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of the public trial and persecution of HCE, the ballad of Hosty, and the testimony of witnesses. During this Age of Gods phase, HCE embodies the patriarch whose guilt, grandeur, and fall drive the cyclical dream forward.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
McHugh, Roland. The Sigla of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/siglaoffinnegans0000mchu
James Joyce Digital Archive: Finnegans Wake Notons. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Liturgical echo "Amen" on page 70 ("The Trial of HCE"): Catholic ritual, Latin prayer, and sacramental language weave through the public trial and persecution of HCE, the ballad of Hosty, and the testimony of witnesses. Joyce fuses ecclesiastical solemnity with domestic banality during the Age of Gods phase, treating the tavern counter as communion rail and the sleeping body as sacred vessel.
sources: Contemporary Literature Press: Classical Lexicon for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro
Frazer, Sir James George. Folk-Lore in the Old Testament. https://archive.org/details/folkloreinoldtes01frazuoft
